Q: Why is gcloud finding an old version of Python? A:

It seems like a known issue with brew itself. I faced it today 22 Feb 2026 as well.

https://dev.to/eunice-js/the-google-cloud-cli-installation-saga-how-i-conquered-python-path-hell-on-macos-3605?utm_source=openai

I fixed with AI by setting

export CLOUDSDK_PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3
brew install --cask google-cloud-sdk

Ref: https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/topic/startup?utm_source=openai

export CLOUDSDK_PYTHON=/usr/local/my-custom-python-install/python

Q: Is it a good practice to declare plugins using id("org.company.myplugin") instead of alias(libs.plugins.myplugin) with version catalogs in Gradle? A:

I wasn't aware of the Now in Android project, so I went to have a look - it's sort of a testing ground for Declarative Gradle.

Yeah, I know, Gradle was already declarative, but not really, because in many cases the order of configuration matters, and this is them trying to sort that out. I'm still a bit upset that they couldn't make the entire build TOML, because that's what I really wanted, but oh well.

But anyway, the reason this matters for the question is: TOML version catalogs were (and may still be) unavailable in Declarative Gradle. That was the case when I checked it out a few months back, and it continues to be the reason why I have been unable to migrate any of my builds to it.

Q: Model context protocol A:

Well, there is Java SDK to develop MCPs. You can find some dość at https://modelcontextprotocol.io/sdk/java/mcp-server

Having that, nie you can implement either local MCP servers or remote.

With local MCP server, you need to develop and then put IT somewhere others can download and install it on their machines. Of course, you would local MCPs use stdio for communication.

With remote MCP server, you need to just deploy your web server with MCP server and make it accessible to your target audience. Remote MCP servers Communicates through HTTP protocol.

Q: VBA Macro for modifying Ribbon produces error A:

I think the problem is a mismatch between the name of the callback sub in your XML and the actual name of the Sub in your VBA module. While VBA is often case-insensitive, the Ribbon XML callback mechanism can be case-sensitive and is very strict about the name.

In the XML you specify onLoad="rxlRibbonUI_onload", but the VBA procedure is named rxIRibbonUI_onLoad. Those must match exactly, including spelling and case (Excel is not case‑sensitive, but the string must be identical).

Your XML specifies: onLoad="rxlRibbonUI_onload"

Your VBA Sub is named: Public Sub rxIRibbonUI_onLoad(...)

Change the onLoad attribute to match the VBA sub name we will create. Let's use a more standard name like OnRibbonLoad.

XML Corrected…

 <customUI xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/2009/07/customui"
onLoad="OnRibbonLoad">
  <commands>
    <command idMso="Cut"
      getEnabled = "rxshared_getEnabled"
    />
    <command idMso="Copy"
      getEnabled = "rxshared_getEnabled"
    />
    <command idMso="Paste"
      getEnabled = "rxshared_getEnabled"
    />
  </commands>
</customUI>

VBA Module Code Corrected

 ' It's best practice to have this in a standard module (e.g., Module1)
' and NOT in a sheet or workbook module.

' Global variable to hold the Ribbon UI object
Public grxIRibbonUI As IRibbonUI

'--- CALLBACK for onLoad ---
' This MUST match the name in the customUI XML's onLoad attribute.
Public Sub OnRibbonLoad(ByRef ribbon As IRibbonUI)
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    ' Set the global ribbon object
    Set grxIRibbonUI = ribbon
    
    ' Optional but recommended: Invalidate the controls to force a refresh
    ' This ensures the getEnabled callback is called immediately.
    grxIRibbonUI.InvalidateControl "Cut"
    grxIRibbonUI.InvalidateControl "Copy"
    grxIRibbonUI.InvalidateControl "Paste"
    
    Exit Sub

ErrorHandler:
    ' This will prevent the "Cannot run the macro" error from showing to the user.
    ' You can log the error or just ignore it.
    Debug.Print "Error in OnRibbonLoad: " & Err.Description
    ' Resume Next is useful here to allow Excel to continue loading.
    Resume Next
End Sub


'--- CALLBACK for getEnabled ---
' This is called by the Ribbon for each control that needs its state (enabled/disabled) updated.
Public Sub rxshared_getEnabled(ByRef Control As IRibbonControl, ByRef returnedVal)
    On Error Resume Next ' Prevent errors in this callback from crashing Excel
    
    Select Case Control.ID
        Case "Cut", "Copy", "Paste"
            ' Set to False to Disable
            returnedVal = False
        Case Else
            ' For any other control, default to enabled
            returnedVal = True
    End Select
End Sub

In my opinion, implementing these changes will cause your ribbon to load correctly, and the Cut, Copy, and Paste buttons will be disabled as desired. I haven't tested it myself, but it should work.

My answer is without guarantee!

I hope it helps you.

Q: Elasticsearch server not accepting connections A:

Check the upper part of your start up log file. Probably, there are other errors printed. In my case too, the last line was about trying to load geoip-databases. Actual root cause was low disk space on the path where data directory was hosted.ElasticSearch version: 7.14.0
